finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws. The return value is ignored, so the OWNER check is never enforced. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant. The name 'requireRole' suggests it enforces, and the javadoc says it does not throw, but the caller treats it as a guard. The sibling export() correctly uses checkRole().
finding.source: Any authenticated user (with or without the OWNER role) calling POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant id.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive operation that deletes tenant data.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the endpoint handler; both parameters are request-controlled
requireRole(u, "OWNER") returns false for non-owners, but the result is discarded and execution continues
requireRole just returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws

finding.guards_checked: Checked for a throwing check (checkRole is used only in export, not wipe), for a return-value check (none), and for a tenant-membership or ownership check (none; the tenant is never compared to the user). No other files exist in the directory, so no upstream filter or middleware is visible. The only authorization in wipe is the ignored requireRole call.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (Admin.java:14) returns a boolean and does not throw. wipe() discards the result at line 26. checkRole (line 18) does throw, but only export() calls it (line 32). There is no tenant-ownership check.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement, and requireRole (Admin.java:14-16) only returns a boolean, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user regardless of role.

verdict_facts.guard_found: requireRole(u,"OWNER") at Admin.java:26 — returns boolean, never throws, result discarded; no other guard (checkRole is only used in export at :32).
verdict_facts.reason: Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing boolean requireRole (defined :14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() which uses throwing checkRole at :32.

finding.claim: Tenant scoping is missing. checkRole only checks that the user holds a global OWNER role. It does not check that the user owns or belongs to the tenant in the path. An OWNER of tenant A can export (and, via F1, wipe) tenant B's data (IDOR / cross-tenant authorization failure). User has no tenant association, so the role cannot be tenant-scoped.
finding.source: Authenticated user holding OWNER on any tenant, supplying another tenant's id in /tenants/{t}/export.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant), which exports the data of a tenant the user does not own.

trace.note: User record has name and roles only, with no tenant binding
export(User u, String tenant), where tenant comes from the URL path
checkRole verifies only that the global role OWNER is present
repo.export(tenant) is called with the unvalidated tenant id

finding.guards_checked: Looked for a tenant-to-user membership check in export() and in checkRole() (none). The roles are plain strings, not tenant-qualified. Only this file is present, so a possible check in the Repo implementation or a gateway could not be verified. This finding depends on a multi-tenant deployment where roles are not tenant-scoped, which the record design suggests.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws SecurityException if the global OWNER role is missing, so it is effective for role presence. No tenant-membership check exists anywhere in the only file present. A gateway or Repo-level check could not be verified.
verdict.reason: User has only name and roles (Admin.java:4), and export() at Admin.java:32-33 checks only the global "OWNER" string before calling repo.export(tenant) with the path-supplied tenant, so an OWNER of any tenant can export another tenant's data, assuming a multi-tenant deployment without checks elsewhere.

verdict_facts.guard_found: checkRole (Admin.java:18-22) throws SecurityException unless the user has the global "OWNER" role. It is a real guard, but it has no tenant scoping. Nothing else is in the directory.
verdict_facts.reason: Admin.java:32 calls checkRole(u,"OWNER"), which checks only for a global role string (Admin.java:19). Admin.java:33 then exports the path-supplied tenant with no membership check, and User (Admin.java:4) has no tenant field, so any OWNER can export any tenant's data.
